headline: Treasuries Retreat as Gains in Equities Sap Demand for Havens
author: Liau Y-Sing

paragraphs.text: Thu, November 26, 2026 at 9:43 PM EST 1 min read
(Bloomberg) -- Treasuries fell in light trading as the market reopened after the Thanksgiving holiday, with gains in Asian equities damping demand for haven assets.

Yields climbed at least three basis points across the curve, with the rate on benchmark 10-year notes up five basis points to 4.90%. A tentative recovery in risk appetite lured investors away from the safety of US government bonds, as regional shares extended a rebound following weeks of volatility in the artificial intelligence trade.

"Positive risk sentiment is the key driver for the tick up in bond yields with the late-session rebound in US technology names on Wednesday flowing through to Asian trade," said Prashant Newnaha, a strategist at TD Securities. "Trading volumes are light ahead of an early 2 p.m. New York close."

US 10-year yields have fallen almost 25 basis points in the past two weeks as traders pared bets for Federal Reserve interest-rate increases after mounting doubts about the AI trade sent stocks tumbling.
